ITEM 3:  DESIGN REVIEW BOARD DRB-25-053
  • 425 North Vega Street
  • Applicant: Gevik Ghazarian
  • Request: This is an application for a new 1,243 SF 2-story addition
  to an existing 1,534 SF 1-story Spanish style single-family residence,
  including the construction of a new attached rear yard trellis.
  • Recommended Action: APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS. The
  proposed project is approved with the following Conditions of
  Approval:
  1. The applicant shall revise the proposed gable vent design to
  a style that is more compatible with the established Spanish
  architectural character of the residence. Appropriate
  alternatives may include, but are not limited to, traditional
  terracotta round vents or decorative vent treatments that are
  consistent with the Spanish architectural style.
  2. The applicant shall revise the proposed roof vent profile and
  color that integrates with the proposed clay tile roofing system.
  Appropriate alternatives may include, but are not limited to, an
  S-profile roof vent design with a color that closely matches the
  adjacent clay tile roofing material, thereby minimizing visual
  contrast and ensuring a cohesive roof appearance.

MOTION:
  •  Moved to continue the application with the following
  recommendations:
  1. The applicant should revise the proposed gable vent design
  to a style that is more compatible with the established Spanish
  architectural character of the residence. Appropriate
  alternatives may include, but are not limited to, traditional
  terracotta round vents or decorative vent treatments that are
  consistent with the Spanish architectural style.
  2. The applicant should revise the proposed roof vent profile and
  color that integrates with the proposed clay tile roofing system.
  Appropriate alternatives may include, but are not limited to, an
  S-profile roof vent design with a color that closely matches the

ITEM 4:  DESIGN REVIEW BOARD DRB-25-059
  • 332 South Chapel Avenue
  • Applicant: Michael Ma
  • Request: This is an application for a new 1,303 SF 2-story addition
  to an existing 665 SF 1-story single-family residence, together with
  an attached 2-car garage.
  • Recommended Action: APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS. The
  proposed project is approved with the following Conditions of
  Approval:
  1. The applicant shall revise the size, proportions, and overall
  scale of the proposed second-floor balcony railing to
  encompass the window trim detailing and to establish a more
  balanced relationship with the covered front porch element
  located directly below.
  2. The applicant shall enhance the architectural detailing of the
  front porch cover by incorporating additional design elements
  characteristic of Spanish Colonial Revival architecture, such
  as a decorative belt courses, horizontal banding, accent trim
  or casing, or decorative tile accents that provides greater
  visual interest and depth to the primary façade.

MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve the application with the following Conditions of
  Approval:
  1. The applicant shall revise the size, proportions, and overall
  scale of the proposed second-floor balcony railing to
  encompass the window trim detailing and to establish a more
  balanced relationship with the covered front porch element
  located directly below.
  2. The applicant shall enhance the architectural detailing of the
  front porch cover by incorporating additional design elements

ITEM 5:  DESIGN REVIEW BOARD DRB-26-034
  • 3112 West Commonwealth Avenue
  • Applicant: Dustyn Howard
  • Request: This is an application for the replacement of the existing
  roofing material on an existing 1-story single-family residence.
  • Recommended Action: CONTINUE. The proposed project is
  continued with the following recommendations:
  1. The applicant should consider utilizing a metal roofing profile
  and/or panel style that closely replicates the appearance and
  texture of traditional shingle or slate roofing materials. A
  roofing system with greater visual similarity to conventional
  residential roofing materials may be more compatible with the
  established character of the surrounding neighborhood and
  better complement the existing Ranch-style architectural
  design of the residence.
  2. The applicant should consider selecting a roofing color that
  provides greater visual contrast with the existing exterior wall
  cladding. Increased differentiation between the roof and wall
  surfaces would enhance the overall architectural composition.
  3. The applicant should provide a detailed roof construction
  detail for the front-facing gable condition, particularly at the
  location where the existing stone veneer projects beyond the
  roof edge. It is recommended that the roof assembly be
  revised to extend beyond the finished face of the wall by a
  minimum of 3” to adequately accommodate a fascia board
  and establish a more conventional roof edge condition.
